newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic crudes trade narrowly, demand intact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic crudes trade narrowly, demand intact.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes traded in narrow ranges over the moderately active session, with support coming from gasoline markets and higher refinery output.
A tight trans-Atlantic arbitrage, where Brent/West Texas Intermediate has come in to $1.25 a barrel for October against $1.40 last Friday, also helped block imports.
Refiners purchased light and heavy cargoes at slightly stronger differentials, with demand attributed to production output amid lean inventories rather than speculation.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $23.40-50 a barrel, up about 20 cents from Wednesday.
Against fewer Iraqi headlines driving direction today, the market focused on fundamentals and Hurricane Fran, churning off the coast of South Carolina.
No major disruptions to refinery operations, however, kept demand intact with speculation that product shipments would be delayed out of Amoco's Yorktown refinery, lending support.
In domestic trade, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James firmed to trade at WTI plus 35 cents, up from 31-34 cents.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire moved at plus 25 cents, up from plus 22 cents previously.
But WTI/Cushing Posting Plus drifted five cents from Wednesday's peak to $2.35 a barrel, in line with softer WTI Oct/Nov spread which also dropped about five cents.
Heavy, sour grades maintained a firm tone with West Texas Sour/Midland inching up five cents to minus $1.17.
Traders said the competition from regional sours was surprisingly not having a bearish impact on domestics.
